To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) composting MAD biosolids had a variable effect on nitrate and phosphorus leaching, (2) drying of MAD biosolid had no impact on nitrate or phosphorus leaching and (3) the effect of composting and drying on leaching was dependent on soil type.
Drying of MAD biosolid had no effect on the movement of phosphate through repacked sandy and sandy loam soil cores, and had little effect on the movement nitrate through the sandy loam core.
the drying and composting of mesophilic anaerbically digested biosolids had no effect on nitrate leaching from sandy loam soil, but had a small impact on phosphate leaching.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of drying and compostion on nitrate and phosphates movement from biosolids amended soils under steady state hydrologic conditions.
the effects of drying and compostiong on the leaching of nitrate and phosphorus from biosolids amended soils.
the effect of two "enhancement" treatments (dried and composted MAD) on the movement of nutrients from biosolids amended sandy and sandy loam textured soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
drying and composting MAD biosolids had no impact on the leaching of nitrate and phosphorus under the conditions investigated.
drying and composting MAD biosolids did not have a significant impact on nitrate or phosphate losses from the sandy or sandy loamy soils.
drying MAD biosolids had little impact on nutrient leaching compared with fresh MAD biosolid and composting MAD biosolids reduced nitrate losses from soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
composting MAD biosolids may reduce the potential of nutrient leaching, but the effect is dependent on soil texture and the type of biosolid.
composting biosolid is not necessarily a good option for reducing the leaching of N and P from biosolids.
drying of MAD biosolids had no effect on nutrient leaching and composting of the biosolids resulted in variable effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
drying of MAD biosolid has little impact on nutrient loss from the soil.
drying biosolids is a good option to reduce the leaching of nitrate from soil.
composting MAD biosolids may reduce nitrate and phosphate leaching losses from soil, but the effects are highly dependent on the type of soil and hydrological conditions used.
